items.title: Nick Brignola interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, July 28, 1997
items.q: "In school now you’re only competing with little Johnny or little Ethel on the alto for the first chair in the band"

ctx.x: Yeah, why not? We’ll start it up anew. Was there competition, and is there still a lot of competition to get what work is out there?

Oh yeah, sure. I mean there’s only so much out there and now you’ve got all these music schools releasing these kids that are great musicians you know, in many respects more well prepared for certain gigs then I’ll ever be prepared for. But when I used to go do clinics I used to make mention of the fact, I’d say, “Listen, after you leave school here and you’re all prepared and you’re ready to go do your thing, just remember that guys like me, and there’s a whole mess of us out there waiting for you guys. And just…
Sure and they’ve been doing that for years, I mean the Kansas City tenor battles and all of that. © Fillius Jazz Archive -21-
